newsitem.title: FRANCE: France ready to back African force in Bangui.
newsitem.headline: France ready to back African force in Bangui.

text.p: France is ready to help an African military force expected to arrive for peacekeeping duties in the Central African Republic in the next few weeks, the Defence Ministry said on Thursday.
Ministry spokesman Pierre Servent said the force of about 300 men from Burkina Faso, Chad, Gabon and Mali would aim to control army mutineers and oversee disarmament efforts.
"France is completely prepared to help the deployment of the African force, which might arrive in coming weeks," Servent told reporters. He gave no details of the French support.

He was answering a question about a statement ascribed to Malian General Amadou Toumani Toure, head of a mediation mission in the Central African Republic, who said the African force would arrive within three weeks and stay about six months.
The capital, Bangui, has been rocked by fighting between opposing army units divided along ethnic lines. Ethnic killings have sparked an exodus of civilians from parts of the city.

Some soldiers are in revolt against the France-backed government for the third time. Mutinies began last April over pay and resurfaced in May as part of a wider campaign to oust President Ange-Felix Patasse, a civilian elected in 1993.
The crisis, in which hundreds of people have been killed, flared anew on November 15 when Yakomas in the army mutinied again. A fragile truce runs out on January 23.
